subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub publicly classify purpose-external agent instructions—especially fetch-and-execute, privilege escalation, confirmation bypass, and undisclosed external actions—as prohibited or review-required, and how should declarations and appeals affect that classification?
rationale: Current internal evaluation already recognizes these risks, but choosing the public normative boundary, exceptions, declaration effect, and arbitration path changes ClawHub’s security and moderation policy.

options.title: Adopt a narrow public rule
options.body: Add purpose-scoped allowed, review-required, and prohibited examples to public policy, with durable moderator guidance and declarations treated as evidence rather than automatic approval.

options.title: Fold into the broader RFC
options.body: Resolve the rule entirely through https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2321 and keep this RFC as supporting threat-model context until that policy lands.

options.title: Keep evaluator-only guidance
options.body: Leave the boundary internal and continue handling agent-directed documentation through case-by-case scanner and moderator judgment.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow public rule
recommendation.body: Add purpose-scoped allowed, review-required, and prohibited examples to public policy, with durable moderator guidance and declarations treated as evidence rather than automatic approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active content-policy RFC already owns the decision about public acceptable-use categories versus reviewer-only guidance.
